correctness.summary: The quantitative lifting lemma is an immediate consequence of additive Cartesian-product distances: layer shifts add the same integer to all three sorted cycle distances, so only equal gap codes can collide, and q-separated heights rule out cancellation across m<=q layers. The explicit cycle tables give all repeated gap-code pairs in twelve parity/residue cases and four boundary families, with every repeated pair separated in height by at least q. This proves the stated three-vertex resolving sets. Exact-integer verification independently recomputed the repeated pairs for q through 500 and directly checked cylindrical codes for m through 30.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Marcelo--Tolentino--Garciano--Buot (2025) prove the prior uniform range n>=8m+1, develop strong m-resolving and gap-code lifting methods, and explicitly leave the remaining cylindrical cases open; those ingredients are credited. The exact prism slice is also prior. A 2026 survey still records the 8m+1 range. Searches under multiset dimension, m-resolving sets, ID-coloring, strong ID-coloring, cylindrical grids, Cartesian products, and equivalent threshold formulations found no 6m-scale three-basis theorem or finite-height quantitative lifting criterion. Residual risk remains from differently phrased older ID-coloring work or very recent unindexed follow-up work.

value.summary: The result lowers the leading constant in the published uniform circumference threshold for multiset dimension three from 8 to 6, adds explicit parity-dependent boundary families, and isolates a reusable bounded-translation lifting principle for Cartesian products with a path.

limitations: The result is a sufficient range, not an exact classification of all cylindrical parameters with multiset dimension three.
The m=2 prism instances are prior work and are not claimed new.
Older ID-coloring formulations and very recent or unindexed parallel work remain residual originality risks.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the symbolic proof.
